item.description:
Terminals kept whole while Wortel is closed, and agents that come back on their own

Wortel 2026.47.4 · 2026-11-20

This update restarts your shells once. Installing it ends every session’s shell and starts a new one, once, because the part of Wortel that keeps them running has changed. Claude Code, Codex and Pi come back by themselves, each in its own conversation, and your shell history is saved as usual. Anything else that was running, like a dev server, needs starting again. If Restart Now does nothing, quit Wortel with ⌘Q to finish the update.

Your terminals are kept whole. Wortel used to rebuild a terminal’s screen when it opened, and that could come back narrow, doubled or in pieces. The process that keeps your shells running now keeps each terminal as well, so after a quit, an update or even a crash a session is exactly as it was, scrollback included, with whatever an agent drew while Wortel was closed. A session out of sight for a minute gives its memory back and returns the same way when you open it.

Agents come back where they were. After a restart each agent resumes its own conversation, even when several share a folder. One you opened and never typed into starts fresh instead of joining someone else’s. An agent that starts while Wortel is closed now tells Wortel what it’s doing, like any other, and so does every agent this update restarts.

Fixes. Restart Now in the update dialog sometimes did nothing. Wortel now quits by itself a few seconds after you click it. Claude Code started through another command, like caffeinate -i claude, now resumes its conversation too.

More than one window, and terminals that come back as you left them

Wortel 2026.47.3 · 2026-11-20

More than one window. Window ▸ New Window (⇧⌘N) opens a second window with a sidebar of its own. Drag a session onto the other window’s sidebar to move it there, or out of the window to give it one of its own; it keeps running as it is. A session’s menu has Move to New Window and Move to Window, and Window ▸ Merge All Windows puts everything back in one. Closing a window closes its sessions, asking first if something is running in them. New Worktree Session is ⌥⇧⌘N now, since ⇧⌘N opens a window.

Your terminals come back as you left them. After you quit or update, a session’s terminal used to start empty and its agent printed what it could again, sometimes narrow or twice over. Every session’s screen and scrollback are now kept when Wortel quits and put back when it opens, before anything else. It starts with the first quit after this update; the update itself comes back the old way. After a crash, the shells are still there and the agent draws its screen again, as before.

Restart agents that were already running. Claude Code and Pi sessions already running when you update won’t show when they’re working until you restart them. They ask whether the terminal is listening only when they start.

Agents say what they’re doing. Claude Code, Codex, Pi, opencode and others now tell Wortel when they’re working, waiting for your approval, asking a question, finished or failed, and Wortel no longer guesses from the title or the screen. A Codex turn that ended no longer arrives as “needs input”.

Smoother, steadier terminals. Resizing the window or dragging the divider keeps up with the pointer. A terminal no longer ends up under the side column after you switch sessions, a session you come back to after a while is no longer drawn in scattered pieces, and agents out of sight work at the width you’ll see them at.

The sidebar sorts. Each section has Sort By in its ”…”: Recent Activity, Date Created, Name, or by hand. Folders come before loose sessions, section headers are easier to read, and pressing the session you’re in puts the keyboard back in its terminal.

Smaller things. ⌘-clicking a path an agent printed opens it in Wortel at its line. A new agent session that would start in your home folder gets a folder of its own in ~/Wortel, and sessions opened at home are called Home. Every terminal follows light and dark at once, and text stays readable when you switch. ⌘O and renaming a folder work again.

Usage data. Wortel now counts when a window is opened, with roughly how many are open, and when sessions move between windows, and how. It still never collects what you type, what your terminals show, or the names of your files, folders or repositories.

New sessions can start your agent, and Wortel has Settings

Wortel 2026.47.2 · 2026-11-18

New sessions start your agent. In Settings, type any command into “New sessions start with”, or pick one of the agents Wortel finds on your Mac from the menu beside the field. Every new session then starts it: ⌘N, ⌥⌘N, ⇧⌘N, ⌘O, a folder’s + and a folder dropped on the sidebar. Session ▸ New Terminal (⌃⌘N) opens one without it, and is there only while the field is filled. Left empty, a new session is a plain terminal, as before. wortel new and the sessions Wortel brings back at launch don’t use it.

Settings. Wortel ▸ Settings… (⌘,) opens a small window with two tabs. General has what new sessions start with, whether Source Control shows its commit box, and whether local servers open in your browser. Updates has automatic updates and anonymous usage data. The menu items Check for Updates Automatically, Share Anonymous Usage Data and Open Servers in Default Browser are gone; their switches are here now. The ⓘ at the bottom of the sidebar still has its usage data switch.

New sessions go on top. A new session outside a folder now goes to the top of the sidebar, so the newest is first. In a folder it goes under the session you’re on.

Idle agents give their memory back. An idle Claude Code holds 130 to 400 MB. When one has finished its turn and its session hasn’t been on screen for an hour, Wortel now ends it and keeps the shell. Select the session and the same conversation is resumed, in a second or two. One waiting on your answer, with something still running under it, with a prompt typed and not sent, or with Remote Control on, gets eight hours instead, and what it started ends with it. A working agent and the session in front of you are never touched. Other agents are left alone for now.

Terminals use less memory. A terminal you haven’t looked at for ten minutes gives back its screen’s memory, about 70 MB each, and has it back when you select it. A leak that grew Wortel by over 100 MB an hour is fixed.

Faster switching. A click on a session switches on mouse-down, as Finder’s sidebar does, and its terminal appears at its final size instead of growing into place.

Smaller things. The sidebar’s toggle and arrows move with it when it opens or closes. A terminal drawn under the side column or in a corner of its pane is now put right as soon as the layout settles. Usage data now counts whether a new session started with a command and which agent was ended or resumed this way, with nothing about the command you typed, the session or the conversation.
